items.title: Wycliffe Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: Victor Goines was improvising and Wes picked up his horn and I picked up my horn at the same time and were just going to play a background.

ctx.x: Oh different things. It could be life experiences. I grew up in the church down south, I was in church every Sunday whether I wanted to be or not. I’d really like to do a Gospel album. I recorded a record on Cris Cross called “The Gospel Truth,” which was hymns and spirituals and a couple of original compositions. But it depends. It comes from many things. But mainly things that are blues based and the feeling I guess of the music of the church. And I think it’s intertwined in many different things. And sometimes…

somewhere on the west coast, some small rural town out in the midwest. And one of the themes that he wrote [scats] and on the radio we was listening to a jazz station, we had about twenty minutes to get to the sound check, and a guitarist comes on playing [scats]. I said okay, well the first four measures, well I was just hearing the same thing. And then he played the next, and again we hadn’t recorded the music, and this was recorded because it was on the radio. And it was almost exactly identical to what Wynton…
I guess there’s some musical ideas floating around out there and people tune into them at the same time.
